clue.text: This religion thins out approaching occident, initially

indicators.note: thins out suggests the letters of the word thins are put out of order
initially points to the opening letter of the word occident

explanation.surface: A faith is said to thin out as it nears the West.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' looks part of the phrase 'thins out' but is the anagram signal; 'approaching' simply places the initial letter of 'occident' at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Japan's native faith, centred on kami spirits, is a religion.

indicators.note: from tells us the letters are taken straight out of the words garden, diverted

explanation.surface: A salad leaf has been rerouted away from a vegetable patch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' signals the run of letters straddling 'garden' and 'diverted'.
explanation.definitionFit: Endive is a leafy chicory relative eaten raw in salads.

indicators.note: a mystery is a puzzle to be worked out, so the title's letters are muddled and must be sorted

explanation.surface: An invitation to read a whodunnit about glue in the Kent town of Dartford.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mystery' looks like part of the book title but signals that THE DARTFORD GLUE is rearranged. 'Dip' is slang for a pickpocket; the answer is the young pickpocket in Dickens's Oliver Twist.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a pickpocket; the Dickens character is the most famous of that trade.

clue.text: England's openers later trouble is intestinal

parts.note: the first two letters of the word England

indicators.note: to trouble something is to stir it up, so the letters of later are disturbed

explanation.surface: England's opening batsmen run into stomach trouble later on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'openers' is a cricket word for the first batsmen, here the first two letters EN; 'trouble' rearranges LATER into TERAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Enteral is the medical adjective for things relating to or passing through the intestine.

clue.text: Gave new business to bank, began a story

definitions.meaning: a customer who brings a bank fresh custom by starting to hold money there
started a narrative or report of events, an account being a telling

explanation.surface: A customer signs up with a bank and starts telling a tale.
explanation.definitionFit: An account is both a banking arrangement and a narrative, so starting either one fits.

parts.note: sent means dispatched or carried off

indicators.note: new tells us the word line appears in a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A guard is moved on to a newly built railway line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transported' suggests carrying but here means dispatched; 'new' is the anagram signal for 'line'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentinel is a soldier or watchman posted to keep watch.

definitions.meaning: people who ditch things, ditching meaning dumping or abandoning
labourers who dig and maintain drainage channels on farmland

explanation.surface: A question whether farm labourers walk out on their jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Ditch means discard and also a drainage trench, so the word names both deserters and trench-digging labourers.

indicators.note: double asks for the word given by feature to appear twice

parts.note: the chin is a feature of the face

explanation.surface: A cinema showing two films back to back is welcomed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'double feature' suggests a cinema bill, but a feature here is a facial feature, written twice.
explanation.definitionFit: A drinking toast or informal salutation used when raising glasses.

indicators.note: not entirely means the word is incomplete, cut short by its final letter

parts.note: precise means accurate

explanation.surface: A digest that is somewhat lacking in accuracy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not entirely' drops the final E of PRECISE.
explanation.definitionFit: A précis is a short abstract giving the main points of a text.

definitions.meaning: to fasten with a knot or cord

explanation.surface: Fasten down a picnic basket.
explanation.definitionFit: To bind fastens something firmly, and being bound also restricts movement.

clue.text: Somehow saving energy at both ends? Fancy!

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters of saving are got into shape in some unexplained way

parts.note: E again, since the clue puts energy at both ends

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise at a scheme to save energy at either end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Somehow' rearranges SAVING into NVISAG; 'at both ends' places an E either side of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Fancy as a verb means imagine or picture, a synonym.

parts.note: taken as written
T as in a T-square, the draughtsman's tool
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: A card player remarks that there are no square diamonds.
explanation.definitionFit: To notice something is to see or spot it, a synonym of observe.

parts.note: budding means developing, not yet realised

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters of garden run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: A gardener fears the menace of an overgrown plot coming into bud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' rearranges GARDEN into DANGER.
explanation.definitionFit: A hazard that might arise is a threat in waiting.

indicators.note: tipped means turned over, so the word for rubbish is read upside down in this down entry

parts.note: rot means nonsense or rubbish

explanation.surface: A heap where rubbish has been dumped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tipped' suggests fly-tipping but turns ROT upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: A tor is a rocky hilltop, especially on Dartmoor in south-west England.

indicators.note: out signals the letters of clue far are put out of place

explanation.surface: A solver suspicious of a clue that seems far-fetched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'far-out' reads as one word, but 'out' is the signal to rearrange CLUE and FAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Being cautious and watchful, a synonym.

clue.text: Nothing lost, presumably, in such a price

definitions.meaning: everything that went missing has turned up again
wages that include free food and lodging on top

explanation.surface: A deal in which all missing items are recovered.
explanation.walkthrough: As a term for pay, it means board and lodging are provided in addition to the wage.
explanation.definitionFit: Taken literally the phrase means every item has been located; as a pay term it means with keep included.

clue.text: Japanese polish, you could say, is one

definitions.text: Japanese polish, you could say, is one

parts.words: Japanese polish, you could say, is one
parts.note: read polish as Polish: someone part Japanese and part Polish has Asian and European ancestry

explanation.surface: A lacquer finish from Japan is described.
explanation.walkthrough: The lower-case 'polish' suggests lacquer; capitalise it and a person of Japanese and Polish descent is of mixed continental heritage.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone of mixed European and Asian parentage is described by this term.

clue.text: National side on the ball in America

definitions.meaning: belonging to the people of England

definitions.text: side on the ball in America
definitions.meaning: in American billiards and pool, spin put on the cue ball

explanation.surface: A national team takes the field in the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: In US pool, sidespin on the ball is called this.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a nationality and, in American cue sports, sidespin.

clue.text: I would contract nothing in artificial language

parts.note: I'd is the contracted form of I would
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone would shrink to nothing inside an invented tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Ido is a constructed language derived from Esperanto.

parts.note: air means appearance or look, as in an air of confidence
to lock is to close fast

explanation.surface: A plumber spots a bubble in a pipe and urges a closer look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close' reads as 'nearby' but is the verb, to shut.
explanation.definitionFit: A trapped pocket of gas blocking flow in a pipe, the question mark marking it as a description.

clue.text: The birds director, we hear-old king taking trouble with rooster

parts.note: Alfred the Great, the ninth-century king of Wessex
a hitch is a snag or trouble
a cock is a male chicken, a rooster

explanation.surface: An ancient monarch takes a cockerel, causing a problem for a film-maker.
explanation.walkthrough: The Birds is the 1963 thriller; 'we hear' is padding that simply joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The British-born filmmaker directed the horror thriller The Birds.

indicators.note: opening of points to the first letter of the word cocktail

parts.note: a lever is a bar used for prising

explanation.surface: A cocktail bar opening is a smart idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' reads as a pub but is a metal lever.
explanation.definitionFit: Bright means intelligent, a synonym.

indicators.note: to design is to shape anew, so the pooled letters are redrawn

explanation.surface: A firm's footwear design has been chosen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'design' rearranges CO and SHOE together.
explanation.definitionFit: To select is to pick or decide on, a synonym.

clue.text: Employed pole outside, being stirred up

indicators.note: outside tells us the word for pole wraps round the other piece

parts.note: a rod is a pole
employed in the sense of put to use

explanation.surface: A worker uses a pole to stir something up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Employed' is loose for the stem use; 'outside' is the container signal, the pole wrapping round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Roused means agitated or excited, matching stirred up as an adjective.

parts.note: loose means not tied or attached
box is a tree and its hard wood

explanation.surface: A section of a building made of wood that has come loose.
explanation.walkthrough: Box is a shrub prized for its dense timber.
explanation.definitionFit: A roomy stall in a stable where a horse can move freely.

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: good means satisfactory, acceptable

explanation.surface: A question whether sloppy emotion is nearly OK.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the D from GOOD.
explanation.definitionFit: Goo is slang for sickly sentiment, mushiness.

indicators.note: at sets the eating word beside the pub word, after it

parts.note: an inn is a tavern
ate means had a meal

explanation.surface: Eating at the pub is the most natural thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at' reads naturally as 'eating at the pub' and doubles as the instruction placing the meal word after the pub word.
explanation.definitionFit: Inborn or inherent qualities are natural ones.

clue.text: Eskimo in a boat, perhaps, is at once in trouble

indicators.note: in trouble suggests the letters of is at once are in disarray

explanation.surface: An Inuit paddler gets into difficulty right away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in trouble' rearranges IS AT ONCE. An Inuit in a kayak is one example of a paddler, so 'perhaps' marks it.
explanation.definitionFit: An Inuit paddling a kayak is an example of a boat-paddler.
